analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן introduces the reason a man leaves his parents and clings to his wife. כֵּן points back to the preceding description of the woman as the man’s own flesh, and עַל marks that as the basis for the statement.
analysis.gloss: on account of (עַל כֵּן, “for this reason”)
analysis.morphology: Preposition without prefix or suffix, followed by כֵּן.

analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן points back to the woman’s origin from the man and presents it as the reason a man leaves his parents and cleaves to his wife.
analysis.morphology: Invariable adverb following the separate preposition עַל in the expression עַל־כֵּן.

analysis.evidence: אִישׁ ‘a man’ is the subject. The two direct-object markers introduce אָבִיו ‘his father’ and אִמּוֹ ‘his mother’. The following וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ ‘and clings to his wife’ places the leaving in the context of marriage. The imperfect expresses a general pattern.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular, with no attached preposition, conjunction, or suffix.
analysis.sense: to leave one’s parents upon marriage

analysis.evidence: אִישׁ is the subject of יַעֲזָב. The verse speaks generally of a man who leaves his father and mother and clings to his wife.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אִישׁ is the subject of יַעֲזָב (“a man leaves”). אֶת introduces אָבִיו (“his father”), which is definite through its possessive suffix. The parallel וְאֶת אִמּוֹ (“and his mother”) marks the second object of the same verb.
analysis.gloss: marks “his father” as the direct object (untranslated)
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in the short form אֶת, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אָבִיו is paired with אִמּוֹ ‘his mother’ as an object of יַעֲזָב ‘leaves’. Both possessive suffixes refer to אִישׁ ‘a man’, identifying the two parents he leaves.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת אָבִיו וְאֶת אִמּוֹ, “his father and his mother” are the two objects of יַעֲזָב, “will leave.” Both possessive suffixes refer to אִישׁ, the man who leaves his parents.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: The subject is אִישׁ, and בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ identifies his wife as the person to whom he clings. Leaving his parents and becoming one flesh with his wife frame the verb as an expression of marital attachment.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וְ. The weqatal continues יַעֲזָב with the same general force.
analysis.sense: to cling to someone in a close, lasting bond

analysis.evidence: In וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ, בְּ marks the person to whom the man clings, and וֹ refers back to אִישׁ. He leaves his father and mother, and the couple become one flesh, identifying her as his wife.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ + feminine singular construct noun אִשְׁתּ־ + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ.

analysis.evidence: The plural וְהָיוּ refers to the man and his wife. After he clings to her, לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד names the resulting state: they become one flesh.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with prefixed וְ in a weqatal sequence

analysis.evidence: The man leaves his parents and clings to his wife. The plural וְהָיוּ refers to the couple, while אֶחָד modifies the singular בָשָׂר. Calling them “one flesh” expresses their new kinship through the image of bodily union.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed לְ marking the result of becoming.

analysis.evidence: After the man clings to his wife, the plural verb וְהָיוּ refers to them both. In לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד, “into one flesh,” אֶחָד describes the unity they come to share.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine singular absolute, modifying בָשָׂר.
analysis.sense: one and the same; made one, united
